codeReview.summary: All five requirements are fully addressed. (1) `build_headless_command()` constructs a list of str arguments (shell=False), which correctly handles Windows paths with spaces. (2) `GHIDRA_HEADLESS_TIMEOUT = 120` is passed through to `subprocess.run(... timeout=timeout ...)`. (3) The old silent mock-data fallback is completely removed; `require_ghidra_available()` raises `GhidraUnavailableError`, caught in `_process_analysis_request()` to return HTTP 503 + `{"error": "Ghidra unavailable"}`. (4) Both `ExportAnalysisJSON.py` and the new `ExportAnalysisJSON.java` populate the `source` field from `getDecompiledFunction().getC()`, and `normalize_analysis_data()` in the server normalizes `source`/`decompiled` fields consistently. (5) `/health` endpoint returns `{"ghidra_available": true/false}` via `get_ghidra_status()`. The code is clean, well-structured, uses proper logging (%-style), and the four unit tests cover health, 503 behavior, Windows command construction, and 120s timeout with source normalization. End-to-end verification against `test_samples/sample.exe` confirmed 99 functions with real decompiled C (first function source length 4217 chars).
